stories.title: Edge sits where fundamentals and price split: memory, aluminum and holiday spending against a CTA-driven, still-fragile tape
stories.summary: Credit is still deteriorating, with HY spreads at 3.72% (96th 3-year percentile, +0.42pt in a month) and the 10Y at 4.91% (94th percentile), even as VIX fell 29% in five days to 25.4. Leveraged funds are not washed out in S&P e-minis (94th percentile net) but are short VIX futures (12th percentile), so a second leg of systematic selling would meet complacent vol positioning.

stories.title: LME aluminum squeeze favors US smelters
stories.summary: LME aluminum stocks are down 51-56% to their lowest since 1990 after the Iran war damaged Gulf smelters, and the cash-to-3-month spread spiked above $250/t. Non-Russian metal is scarce, which feeds premiums that US producers capture. (survived the red team)

cards.title: Observation and edge
items: Consensus: Industrial metals weak; copper -15.2% in a month on growth fears.
The feed says: Aluminum is a supply story; LME stocks -51% since February, nearly all Russian metal.
Edge: The broad metals selloff hides an aluminum-specific physical shortage. Gulf smelter damage takes months to fix, and the feed's sources are primary inventory data.
Priced in? No producer prices in data; copper -15.2% in 1 month masks it
